purpose: Every number printed in the documents listed under `scope` resolves here to the raw result file, the exact command, the dataset, the sample size and the caveats that belong with it. A claim with no entry is a claim with no evidence. Task B2 renders the documents from this file so the two cannot drift.

excludes: fenced code blocks - shell commands and illustrative terminal output, not measurements

nevertwice_history_150.name: the 150 most recent commits reachable from master at 7ef8ad2, each against its parent

One repository by one author: a budget derived from it describes it.

external_heldout_v1.name: nevertwice external held-out v1 - 408 synthetic memory notes over three public domains never trained on, with a twin axis and two retrieval query shapes
external_heldout_v1.note: Exists because the shipped embedding headline (recall 0.220 -> 0.475 at 1% FPR) was measured on the owner's private vault and is therefore unreproducible by anyone else. Frozen at sha256 272cca36b1ab2a28..., checked by `python research/embed_universal/heldout_set.py --verify` and by tests/_test_heldout_set.py. Built from rust-lang/book, arXiv quant-ph abstracts and one Project Gutenberg title; NO material from the store. The lessons were written by a local qwen2.5:7b over ~2 GB of fetched public source, so the corpus itself cannot be regenerated byte-identically from a fresh clone - the set is frozen and its generators are hashed into its manifest instead. 284 English and 124 Russian documents, because the store this serves is bilingual.

supersession_v1.name: Supersession v1
supersession_v1.citation: written for this repository; no external source
supersession_v1.ground_truth: marker strings fixed in the generator before any arm ran; a returned item is a stale assertion only if it carries a retracted marker and no current marker
supersession_v1.note: The cases are authored here rather than scraped, which is a weaker instrument than an external corpus. The naive append-only arm is the guard: it scores 0.950 stale, so the task is not trivially easy.

cheap_baselines.name: matched-condition guard corpus (F2)
cheap_baselines.sha256_note: committed in the repository; the artifact records the corpus counts it ran on
cheap_baselines.ground_truth: single-label top-1, written by the same author as the notes
cheap_baselines.note: n is small and single-author. It supports a precision/recall CURVE and a matched-FPR comparison; it does not support a population estimate.; The paraphrases are written by the same author as the notes. That biases toward recall - a real user's phrasing would share fewer content words. The negatives are the guard against reading too much into that: they are drawn from ordinary work in the same repository and vocabulary.; Ground truth is single-label top-1. An episode heading toward two past failures at once is not represented.

longmemeval_oracle_pinned.name: LongMemEval-oracle, global pool, content-pinned
longmemeval_oracle_pinned.citation: Wu et al., LongMemEval: Benchmarking Chat Assistants on Long-Term Interactive Memory, ICLR 2025
longmemeval_oracle_pinned.ground_truth: human-annotated answer_session_ids, independent of this project's embeddings
longmemeval_oracle_pinned.note: Not committed - 15 MB of third-party data - but pinned by content hash in source, which is the half that was missing when the 2026-07 figures were withdrawn. The harness verifies the hash before it reads a byte and refuses to run on a different file. Every question retrieves from all 940 unique sessions rather than its own evidence set, which is what makes the oracle variant a retrieval task.

longmemeval_s_pinned.name: LongMemEval-S, global pool, content-pinned
longmemeval_s_pinned.citation: Wu et al., LongMemEval: Benchmarking Chat Assistants on Long-Term Interactive Memory, ICLR 2025
longmemeval_s_pinned.note: The standard non-oracle variant: 19,829 unique haystack sessions, twenty-one times the oracle pool. This is the setting the roadmap meant by 'outside the oracle setting'. 623 of the 19,829 unique session ids carry no text at all in the published corpus and cannot be embedded, so the retrievable pool is 19,206. That is a property of the dataset, recorded here so the pool size is not read as a loading failure.

locomo10_pinned.name: LoCoMo, ten conversations, content-pinned
locomo10_pinned.citation: Maharana et al., Evaluating Very Long-Term Conversational Memory of LLM Agents, ACL 2024
locomo10_pinned.licence: CC-BY-NC-4.0 per the dataset card; the repository's LICENSE.txt is the authority
locomo10_pinned.ground_truth: human-annotated evidence turn ids (`dia_id`) per question
locomo10_pinned.note: Nine of the 1,986 questions are unscoreable for retrieval and are dropped: four carry no annotated evidence and five name a turn absent from their conversation. Turn ids restart at D1:1 in every conversation, so every id here is namespaced with its conversation - keying anything by the bare id merges ten dialogues into one, which is a defect this stand shipped with for exactly one run.

supersession_v1_implicit.name: Supersession v1, implicit-replacement variant
supersession_v1_implicit.citation: written for this repository; no external source
supersession_v1_implicit.ground_truth: the same marker strings as v1; only the second session's frame differs
supersession_v1_implicit.note: The same facts, markers and queries as supersession_v1; the replacing session is framed like any first assertion (no retraction cue), rotated so the two sessions never share a frame - how a real transcript delivers a replacement (ledger H7/I5). Generated byte for byte by the committed script; `--check` verifies the hash.

research/invariants_lab/DB_AUTHORITY.md.note: Tasks B1-B3 of the invariants lab: migration reversibility and a destructive-operation authority boundary, measured by attack rather than by precision per PREREGISTRATION.md section 6. Fifteen bypass attempts across six classes are published in full with their verdicts; two of them broke earlier builds of the mechanism and are described. Every number regenerates from tests/_test_db_authority.py, which is hermetic.

research/invariants_lab/DEFECTS.md.note: Phase D of the invariants lab: the five false-positive classes the previous census quantified and left in the code, with the state of each. Its shares are quoted from research/blast_radius_precision.json, the artifact of the run being replaced; its regressions live in tests/_test_blast_radius.py and run in CI. D5 is blocked while any row is open, so this page is a gate rather than a claim.

research/invariants_lab/BLAST_RADIUS_D5..note: Task D5 of the invariants lab: precision AND recall for the blast-radius checker on the eight-repository corpus, against git grep at a matched flag rate, with every threshold fixed in PREREGISTRATION.md before the run. Two of four gates fail and the mechanism is deleted; the numbers regenerate from research/invariants_lab/measure_blast_radius.py against blast_radius_d5.json and the SHAs in corpus_manifest.json. Every finding is judged mechanically, never by hand, and the 70% abstention rate is reported with the precision it qualifies.

research/invariants_lab/HELDOUT_V.md.note: Phase V of the invariants lab: every mechanism measured once on twenty-seven repositories the frozen code never saw, against thresholds fixed in PREREGISTRATION-SHIP.md before the corpus was cloned. blast_radius under decidable-only passes all three V1-A gates out of sample; the ratchet, scale's static half and the union fail theirs and are deleted per their declared consequences. The numbers regenerate from research/invariants_lab/analyse_v.py against v_delta.json and the *_heldout.json artifacts run_phase_v.py produced. Provenance of each artifact is established in PROVENANCE_V.md from the data rather than the labels, because three of them are mislabelled.

research/invariants_lab/PROVENANCE_V.md.note: The provenance audit that had to run before any Phase V number was interpreted: three artifacts written by the unattended chain carry a hardcoded corpus_dev label under a *_heldout.json name. Ten of eleven artifacts are decided from their own contents by three routes - disjoint block names, census shape, and exclusion against the development run - and every decided one is held out. The numbers regenerate from research/invariants_lab/provenance_audit.py against provenance_v.json. The frozen modules are deliberately not edited; the correction lives here with its evidence.

research/invariants_lab/CORPUS.md.note: Task C1 of the invariants lab: the corpus of eight public repositories, its selection rationale committed before any clone, and the census that shows a non-zero base rate. Its numbers are counts of a corpus that lives outside git at D:/Coding/_nevertwice_polygon/corpus and are reproducible from research/invariants_lab/corpus_census.py against the SHAs in corpus_manifest.json; nothing here is a claim about the product. Registering them as claims waits for Phase T, when the lab results are either promoted or published as negatives.

research/invariants_lab/INVARIANT_NOTES..note: Tasks I1-I3 of the invariants lab: the invariant note type, its two-strike lifecycle, and the three-checker preconfigured pack. Mechanism 1 is infrastructure, judged by contract assertions rather than precision per PREREGISTRATION.md section 7; every claim here is checked by tests/_test_invariant_notes.py, which is hermetic and needs neither vault nor corpus. No claim is made that the pack is useful -- that is T3.

research/invariants_lab/MUTANTS.md.note: Task C2 of the invariants lab: the positive class, 495 breakages generated by reverting the caller half of a commit that changed a signature and updated its callers together. Every one is re-decided by CPython inspect.Signature.bind in verify_mutants.py rather than by the generator that proposed it, and the counts are reproducible from mutants.json and mutant_controls.json against the SHAs in corpus_manifest.json. Nothing here is a claim about the product; the detector measurements land in Phase D.

research/invariants_lab/COLDSTART_T3.md.note: Task T3 of the invariants lab, the cold-start axis: the preconfigured pack measured on the LIVE_VALIDATION stand against two local models, 96 usable generations each. It fails on both, because the base pitfall rate is at or near zero -- the finding being that portable knowledge is the knowledge models already have. Numbers regenerate from research/invariants_lab/measure_coldstart.py against coldstart_t3_qwen35_4b.json and coldstart_t3_qwen25_3b.json; the run was read-only against the owner's already-running Ollama.

research/invariants_lab/README.md.note: Task T5 of the invariants lab: the write-up that ties the six mechanisms together. Every number on it is quoted from one of the per-mechanism documents registered beside it and regenerates from the harness that produced it. Two mechanisms passed their gates, four did not, and the cross-cutting finding -- that scope rather than accuracy is what buys silence -- is stated as an observation across five measured flag rates rather than as a law.

research/invariants_lab/TOGETHER_T1.md.note: Tasks S1-S3, T1 and T2 of the invariants lab: the seam journal executed on a real migration, and the union of every mechanism that passed its own gate measured against the combined flag-rate ceiling declared in PREREGISTRATION.md section 8. The union fails at 0.119, and the declared remedy is applied and its cost reported rather than renegotiated. Numbers regenerate from research/invariants_lab/measure_together.py against together_t1.json; the seam journal claims are checked by tests/_test_seam_journal.py, which is hermetic.

research/invariants_lab/SCALE_X4.md.note: Task X4 of the invariants lab: the scale detector and the 10x canary, the first mechanism to pass all its declared gates. Its static recall and false-positive figures are measured against templates written alongside the detector and the write-up says so in its first paragraph; the non-circular evidence is the dynamic canary and an exploratory flag rate on 738 real corpus commits. Numbers regenerate from research/invariants_lab/measure_scale.py against scale_x4.json.

research/invariants_lab/RATCHET_R3.md.note: Tasks R1-R3 of the invariants lab: the complexity ratchet, measured by agreement with an independent instrument rather than by recall against its own metric, which would be 1.0 by construction. One gate of four fails and the mechanism is deleted. Numbers regenerate from research/invariants_lab/measure_ratchet.py against ratchet_r3.json and the SHAs in corpus_manifest.json; the metric itself is pinned against ruff C901 on every module in nevertwice/ by tests/_test_complexity.py.

research/invariants_lab/POWER.md.note: Task C3 of the invariants lab: what effect sizes the corpus can resolve, computed before any mechanism is measured. Exact binomial for one proportion and simulated exact McNemar for the paired detector-vs-baseline comparison; reproducible from research/invariants_lab/power.py against mutants.json and corpus_census.json. Every number is a minimum detectable effect at a fixed n, never observed power. Nothing here is a claim about the product.

research/invariants_lab/PREREGISTRATION..reason: Task C4 of the invariants lab: the thresholds, baselines and deletion decisions for all six mechanisms, declared before any of them is measured. Its numbers are PROSPECTIVE -- floors, ceilings, required sample sizes and the n each gate will be evaluated at -- not measurements to reproduce, which is the same governance the earlier BLAST_RADIUS_DECISION.md carries for the same reason. The measurements land in the per-mechanism documents of Phase D onward.

research/BLAST_RADIUS_CALIBRATION.md.note: A research write-up, registered the way every other one here is. Its six load-bearing numbers - the ones the T1/T2 decision rests on - are registered as claims and checked against the artifact by tests/_test_blast_radius_calibration.py, which also re-checks the thresholds themselves. research/BLAST_RADIUS_DECISION.md.reason: the decision rules for whether the blast-radius checker is worth keeping, declared before any finding was labelled and before the baseline was built, per hard rule 2.6. The measurements land in research/BLAST_RADIUS_PRECISION.md.

research/BLAST_RADIUS_PRECISION.md.note: the negative result that closed the blast-radius track. Its headline - 0 of 24 findings true, precision 0.000 - is registered as a claim and checked against research/blast_radius_precision.json; the taxonomy of why each finding is false is the backlog. The labeller that produced the labels has its own controls in tests/_test_blast_radius_labeller.py, because a null result whose instrument was never shown capable of a positive is unfalsifiable.

research/EMBED_HELDOUT_BASELINE.md.note: the first evaluation of the shipped embedding on material outside the owner's vault. Its three load-bearing results are registered as claims and checked against research/embed_universal/heldout/baseline_v1.json by tests/_test_heldout_baseline.py; the full table is the backlog. Every per-query rank and per-pair score is in the artifact, so any cell can be recomputed rather than trusted.

research/EMBED_M2_THRESHOLD.md.reason: the success threshold and deletion decision for hard-negative mining, declared before any negative was mined and before anything was retrained, per hard rule 2.6. Its numbers are prospective decision rules - a paired interval that must exclude zero, a bound on collateral regression, and the effect size this benchmark can resolve - not measurements to reproduce. The retrospective figures it cites as motivation are claims already registered from M1.

research/EMBED_HARD_NEGATIVES.md.note: the negative result that closed M2. The gate it failed and the one improvement it did produce are registered as claims and checked against research/embed_universal/heldout/hard_v1.json by tests/_test_hard_negatives.py; the mining statistics and the taxonomy of why are the backlog. The mined checkpoint was deleted per the decision written before the run; every measurement it produced is kept.

research/EMBED_M3_THRESHOLD.md.reason: the success threshold and deletion decision for cross-encoder distillation, declared before any teacher score was collected and before anything was retrained, per hard rule 2.6. Its numbers are prospective decision rules and the effect size the benchmark can resolve, not measurements. The retrospective figures it cites are claims already registered from M1.

research/EMBED_DISTILLATION.md.note: the negative result that closed M3. research/EMBED_M4_THRESHOLD.md.reason: the success threshold and deletion decision for Matryoshka representations, declared before anything was trained or truncated, per hard rule 2.6. Its numbers are prospective decision rules - a bound on what the full vector may lose, tolerances for graceful truncation, and the resolution the benchmark offers - not measurements. It inverts the question M2 and M3 asked, and says so before the run: here 'no accuracy gain, three quarters of the memory' is a pass.

research/EMBED_MATRYOSHKA.md.note: what Matryoshka training bought (nothing measurable) and what the baseline it was measured against revealed (the shipped model already truncates). research/EMBED_M5_THRESHOLD.md.reason: the promotion rule and deletion decision for the LoRA capacity sweep, declared before any rank was trained, per hard rule 2.6. research/EMBED_M6_THRESHOLD.md.reason: what the served model had to prove before its numbers could be quoted as the shipped model's, declared before a single embedding was fetched. research/invariants_lab/ENDTOEND_HELDOUT.note: The shipping gate re-run out of sample: 150 benefit and 150 harm trials on the held-out corpus, 87 usable pairs against the 37 PREREGISTRATION-SHIP.md required. claims.caveat: It repairs a regression v1 carried against stock on an axis where every model already exceeds 0.95, so it cannot matter to the product. The negatives were mined from other lessons' rewrites, which are near-duplicate NOTES - the title-axis skill - and no negative had the shape of a situation query.

claims.statement: distilling the cross-encoder costs 0.056 of situation recall@5 against the shipped model, 95% interval [-0.102, -0.009] - a measured regression, not an unresolved improvement
claims.ci_note: percentile bootstrap, 2000 resamples, seed 20260827, on the per-query difference so the pairing is kept. The interval excludes zero on the wrong side.
claims.caveat: The teacher is WORSE than the student at recall@1 and better at recall@5; distilling its full ranking transfers both. This is a result about this teacher distilled this way, not about distillation. The checkpoint was deleted per the deletion decision; v1 remains shipped.

claims.statement: distilling the cross-encoder costs 0.101 of title recall@1 against the shipped model, 95% interval [-0.132, -0.066], five times the regression the guard allowed
claims.ci_note: percentile bootstrap, 2000 resamples, seed 20260827, paired. McNemar 5 won / 46 lost.
claims.caveat: The guard this breaches was written before the run BECAUSE the teacher's own recall@1 is worse than the student's - the mechanism was predicted and then observed. An earlier attempt was worse still (title recall@1 0.797) because the target was on a scale a cosine margin cannot express; that run is reported as a specification error, not as evidence.

claims.statement: the shipped nevertwice-embed truncates to 256 dimensions for 0.060 of situation recall@5, quartering the index without retraining
claims.ci_note: percentile bootstrap, 2000 resamples, seed 20260827, paired against the same model's own full vector. Truncation is prefix-then-renormalise, which is what an index does.
claims.caveat: Measured on 408 documents; an index's difficulty grows with its size, so the cost at a realistic store size is not established here. The title axis moves 0.005 and the twin axis not at all (AUC 1.000 at every width). At 512 dimensions the cost is 0.028.

claims.statement: Matryoshka training truncates to 256 dimensions at exactly the same cost as naive truncation of the shipped model - 0.060 either way - so the training bought nothing measurable
claims.ci_note: percentile bootstrap, 2000 resamples, seed 20260827, paired.
claims.caveat: This also misses the declared K2 tolerance of -0.06 by 0.0002, which is a bright line and is not rounded across - but the decision is the same either way, because the naive baseline is identical. 216 queries resolve about five points, so a real one- or two-point difference between the two models would be invisible here and is not excluded. bge-m3's representation appears already front-loaded, which is the property Matryoshka training exists to create.

claims.statement: at 64x the LoRA rank the model is 0.028 WORSE on situation recall@5 than the shipped r16, 95% interval [-0.060, 0.000] - more capacity buys less on 1463 training pairs
claims.ci_note: percentile bootstrap, 2000 resamples, seed 20260827, paired.
claims.caveat: The curve falls monotonically past r4 (0.838, 0.815, 0.806 for r4/r16/r64), which is what overfitting looks like on this corpus size. No arm cleared the promotion rule, so all four checkpoints were deleted; r4 is where the evidence points if a future run wants a rank.

claims.statement: re-running v1's own recipe - same pairs, loss, epochs, batch, lr, seed, rank - lands 0.018 below the shipped checkpoint on situation recall@5, 95% interval [-0.042, 0.000]
claims.ci_note: percentile bootstrap, 2000 resamples, seed 20260827, paired.
claims.caveat: Inside the noise, and beside the point: it means nevertwice-embed v1 is a particular CHECKPOINT rather than a reproducible artifact. Library versions have moved since it was trained and GPU non-determinism does the rest. The model card must say the recipe reproduces the method, not the weights.

claims.statement: the f16 GGUF Ollama serves agrees with the safetensors checkpoint every published number was measured on to a median cosine of 1.0, with no vector below 0.99 out of 2412
claims.ci_note: a full comparison over every text in the frozen set, not a sample - the distribution is published instead of an interval.
claims.caveat: Stock bge-m3 served the same way shows the same agreement (median 1.0001), so this is a property of the conversion pipeline rather than of this checkpoint. Every retrieval query also ranks identically through both paths.

claims.statement: the served path costs 37 ms per text against 6 ms locally - about six times slower, and it is the path the product takes
claims.ci_note: a single timed pass over 2412 texts; it measures this machine and this batch size.
claims.caveat: Part of the gap is HTTP and batching rather than the model, and this run does not separate them - it measures what a caller experiences. Local was batch 64 through sentence-transformers, served was batch 32 through Ollama's API.

claims.statement: Nevertwice (api.as_of over belief intervals) answers BOTH days correctly on the supersession corpus asked as of a day in 0.800 of cases
claims.note: As-of recall (ledger I6): the sixty supersession cases ingested with dates two months apart through the public API, then asked twice - for a day between the two sessions and for a day after the second. A case counts only when BOTH answers are right: the superseded fact for the old day, with the replacement absent, and the replacement for the new day. Our arm pools two ingest runs (the extractor is not deterministic); the naive floor has no notion of a date, so one ranking answers both days. Mem0 records a blocker: its memories carry the wall-clock time of the add() call and its search has no as-of filter. The gate written before the run was 0.80; this family is below it and is published for that reason.

external_citations.statement: Mem0 reports 91.6 on LoCoMo, which its own analysis says drops to about 49% effective at 50k sessions
external_citations.note: Quoted, not measured here. It is cited to argue that R@k has stopped discriminating, never as evidence about Nevertwice.

external_citations.statement: the effective-accuracy drop is reported at 50k sessions
plain BM25 is reported to score about 94% on LoCoMo's answer-accuracy setting, which is the figure this project's exclusion was written around
external_citations.source: widely reported in the agent-memory literature and vendor write-ups; the exclusion in ROADMAP.md predates this register entry
external_citations.note: Quoted, never measured here. It concerns judge-scored ANSWER ACCURACY. This repository measures LoCoMo retrieval instead, where the term-overlap floor reads 0.499 at R@5 - a different quantity on a different scale, and the two must never appear in one table.

non_metrics.reason: single digit - table headers (R@1, R@3, R@5), k values, list markers and the literal zeros in '0 dependencies' and '0 tokens until they fire'. Too ambiguous to bind to a claim; task B2 generates these positions instead of matching them.
a year - dates such as 2026-07, not a measurement
a Python version in the support matrix
percent-encoded fragment of the LongMemEval badge label ('%20›%200.76')
the month fragment of an ISO date such as 2026-07
the k in the 'R@10' and 'k=10' table positions
percent-encoding fragments inside a badge URL; the badge's human-readable claim is covered by its own claim entry
the count of headline claims, baselines and pairs, tallied by the renderer from this manifest rather than measured
a verdict tally in the generated baseline summary, counted by the renderer from this manifest
the Mem0 release under test - a version string, tokenised as 2.0 and 19
the digits of BM25, the name of a ranking function; covered until 2026-09 by a live claim that happened to print 25%
the length of the recall demo in seconds - a description of a script, not a measurement
the version inside the model name 'qwen2.5-7b-64k', the local model every full-pipeline arm extracted with

the month or day of an ISO date on the same line - not a measurement. Accounted for only by coincidence until 2026-09: whichever claim happened to print the same two digits covered it, and withdrawing that claim exposed the date.

drift_note: A drift entry records a number a document prints that the stored raw result contradicts. All five entries opened by task B1 were closed by task B2: the tables are generated from this manifest now, and the prose around them was corrected to the stored values. Open a new entry when a published figure is found to disagree and cannot be corrected in the same change; the test fails once the document no longer prints it, so an entry cannot outlive its fix.

baseline_policy.rule: A headline is publishable only when it clears every applicable baseline below under matched conditions. A baseline that was not run is recorded as `not_compared`, never omitted: an unrun baseline is the most likely explanation a reader will reach for.
matched_conditions: equal reader model - the same LLM answers in both arms
equal context-token budget - neither arm is allowed more room
equal latency tier - a baseline is not handicapped by being run slower
matched false-positive rate - an intervention that fires more often is not better, it is louder; compare at the same FP rate or report the full curve

verdicts.beats: measured, under matched conditions, and the claim wins
verdicts.ties: measured and within the interval of the baseline
verdicts.loses_to: measured and the baseline wins - the claim must be narrowed or dropped
verdicts.not_compared: not measured yet; the claim is provisional against this baseline
verdicts.not_applicable: the baseline cannot be constructed for this metric; a reason is required

baseline_policy.evidence_rule: A measured verdict (beats / ties / loses_to) must name where the comparison lives: a raw result file, or the claim ids of the two arms. A verdict without evidence is an assertion, and flipping `not_compared` to `beats` must therefore cost something.

no_memory.name: no memory
no_memory.definition: the same agent, same task, with the memory system switched off
no_memory.why: the floor. Any memory that cannot beat its own absence is overhead.
no_memory.how: run the harness with the memory arm disabled

full_history.name: full-history injection
full_history.definition: paste the entire accumulated history into the context instead of retrieving
full_history.why: the dumb baseline that often wins when the history is small; it is what a user does by hand before installing anything.
full_history.how: python research/token_ab.py (the `net vs the full history` column)

lexical_recall.name: lexical recall (BM25)
lexical_recall.definition: term-overlap retrieval with no embedder and no model
lexical_recall.why: zero-dependency, zero-latency, and repeatedly close to far more complicated systems. LoCoMo was discredited partly because BM25 nearly won it.

curated_agents_md.name: a curated AGENTS.md
curated_agents_md.definition: one hand-written instructions file that a person maintains
curated_agents_md.why: the honest competitor for most of what agent memory claims. If a human writing five lines gets the same prevention, the machinery is not earning its place.

llm_session_summary.name: an LLM session summary
llm_session_summary.definition: ask the model to summarise the session and inject that summary next time
llm_session_summary.why: the cheapest possible 'memory', available in one prompt with no system at all
llm_session_summary.how: python research/cheap_baselines.py - **arm built, run GATED**: it runs against a deterministic extractive summariser, never against a model, and is reported as `session_summary_extractive`

linter_or_test.name: the relevant linter or test
linter_or_test.definition: the existing static check that already catches the same class of mistake
linter_or_test.why: several guard-shaped pitfalls (f-string SQL, bare except, missing close) are caught by ruff, bandit or a unit test. A guard that duplicates a linter is not memory, it is a worse linter.
linter_or_test.how: python research/cheap_baselines.py (the `linter_or_test` row) - **built, F2**, as an oracle upper bound on static analysis

curated_haystack.name: an already-curated small haystack
curated_haystack.definition: the handful of sessions that actually contain the answer, pasted whole
curated_haystack.why: stricter than full-history injection at small scale, and this project already runs it. Recording only the six the policy names would hide the harder test.
curated_haystack.how: python research/token_ab.py (the `net vs a curated small haystack` column)

withdrawal.what_happened: Every claim in this manifest carried commit 05cfdc96 - the commit that last *touched the artifact file*, which was a directory move, not the commit whose code produced the number. B1/B2 had closed document-to-artifact drift and left artifact-to-code drift wide open, so the published corpus described the v1.0.0 engine after four rounds of review had rewritten the ranker beneath it.
withdrawal.what_was_done: Each claim now carries `produced_by`, the repository files its command imports, and tools/check_freshness.py fails when any of them changed after the claim's commit. Artifacts whose generators run here - CPU, no key, no gated dataset - were regenerated at HEAD and restamped. The rest are withdrawn: kept in this file with a reason, removed from every published document.
withdrawal.how_to_restore: python tools/check_freshness.py --list-stale names each withdrawn number and its gate. Clearing a gate means committing the dataset with a hash, spending the gated API budget, or running on the owner's own store - then re-running the claim's `command` and restamping `commit`.
